findings.title: Cancel imminent reminders immediately instead of waiting for cron
findings.body: Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, cancelling a booking five minutes before its reminder is due leaves the email scheduled in SendGrid until after it is sent. The cron also deletes past-due reminder rows before processing cancellations, so it cannot recover this case. Reminders close to their send time need immediate provider cancellation.

findings.title: Await reminder cancellations before completing the request
findings.body: The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled-flag update, but their promises are discarded inside forEach and are not included in the awaited promises below. Previously the database reminder deletions were explicitly awaited. The handler can therefore return success before cancellation is persisted; in a serverless deployment, execution can stop after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect and await these helper promises, including the equivalent request-reschedule and workflow-update call sites.

findings.title: Keep immediate cancellations recoverable when SendGrid rejects them
findings.body: The immediateDelete path still submits cancellations arbitrarily far ahead of the send date, which consumes the same 100 pending-cancellation slots described in this PR. handleNewBooking uses this path for every reschedule. If SendGrid rejects a cancellation because that limit is reached, the error is swallowed and the reminder is never marked cancelled, so cron will not retry it and the old booking's email will still be sent. Workflow and step deletion also use this path and then cascade-delete the reminder rows, losing any retry opportunity.

findings.title: Persist successful cancellations before another request can fail
findings.body: The Prisma delete promises accumulated in the loop are lazy and execute only at Promise.all after every SendGrid cancellation succeeds. If any provider request fails, control jumps to the outer catch and none of the earlier successfully cancelled reminders are deleted. On subsequent runs those batches are submitted again; an already-cancelled batch can itself be rejected by SendGrid, repeatedly aborting processing before later reminders are reached. Handle failures per reminder and persist each successful cancellation independently so one failed batch cannot block all remaining cancellations.
